name: Arthur Balfour
role: British prime minister (1902–1905), Irish chief secretary and foreign secretary
summary: Balfour combined imperial unionism and coercive Irish administration with land reform and qualified constitutional adaptation. He supported a Jewish national home in Palestine, limited women’s enfranchisement, publicly aided religious education and conditional tariff reform; his philosophical writing defended theism.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: In Economic Notes he rejects the presumption that the economically natural is better than the state-contrived, and abandons laissez-faire as an absolute dogma, while still calling himself a free trader.

public-ownership.rationale: In his 1924 Peebles speech he warns that placing vast tracts of industry in the grip of a Whitehall bureaucracy, with a capital levy, would bring ruin, and holds up Soviet nationalisation as a failed experiment.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He thinks the 1909 super-tax on about 10,000 persons inexpedient and a risk to capital, though he finds it not arbitrary and prefers it to higher death duties.

property-fundamental.rationale: He attacks the 1909 land duties for spreading insecurity over property legitimately acquired under the law and calls the Welsh disendowment a robbing of the Church.

empower-police-military.rationale: He defended police repression and ordered military assistance with Irish evictions.

decide-locally.rationale: In 1913 he says he is not disposed to agree that a large delegation of parliamentary power to subordinate assemblies would be a great constitutional reform.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: In 1925 he says no community has flourished that was faithless to its own past, while disowning slavish conformity.

gradual-change.rationale: He calls the Socialist programme a complete revolution that tears up continuity, and says institutions in England have grown, not been cut down and replanted; reform must follow the past.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He personally defends excluding immigrants unable to support themselves and others he considers detrimental.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He wanted the League's prestige and power to grow, but rejected giving it forces or turning it into a super-State, and spoke of international sanction in 1917.

free-trade.rationale: He accepts free interchange as an ideal but seeks exceptions for imperial preference and retaliation against foreign barriers.

open-borders.rationale: He explicitly defends a country’s authority to decide whom to admit and under what conditions.

central-planning.rationale: He argues in the same speech that the Soviet system of state ownership and direction failed from every point of view and destroyed capital, credit and production.

tax-inheritance.rationale: He dislikes the increased 1909 death duties, which he says can now only be paid out of capital, and regrets that.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He advocates tariff bargaining powers against foreign measures threatening British and colonial industries, rather than unconditional protection.

widespread-small-property.rationale: His constructive Irish reforms promoted tenant land purchase and improvement of small holdings.

democracy-best.rationale: He calls democracy the only possible government at Britain’s political stage, while limiting its applicability elsewhere.

direct-votes.rationale: In 1911 he says the referendum has an enormous advantage in isolating one question, and in 1910 he offered to put tariff reform to one and urged the government to put Home Rule to one.

right-to-secede.rationale: In 1913 he says no Dominion would tolerate the severance of its territory, that the United States fought its bloodiest war to avoid it, and that welded unions cannot be unloosened. His later reluctant acceptance of the 1921 treaty softens it to -1.

war-builds-character.rationale: In 1920 he says anyone who thinks war improves morality should reflect within the boundaries of an asylum.

separate-church-state.rationale: He opposed the Welsh disestablishment bill as destroying an ancient institution and defended the Church's endowments.

military-superiority.rationale: In 1916 he says Britain and America should keep their maritime power, and that the sanction behind peace must largely be the potential use of sea-power.

self-interest-moral.rationale: He rejects reducing altruism and patriotic sacrifice to disguised personal advantage.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He frames the choice of an economic system as which one gives the best results for the mass of people and points to the experiment of Russia as the test.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He advocates a Jewish national home, not expressly sovereign statehood; its ultimate constitutional meaning remained ambiguous.

national-self-determination.rationale: He backs nationality claims in Europe in 1917 (Alsace-Lorraine, Italia irredenta, Turkish rule over alien races) but says in 1920 nationality is no absolute principle, minorities must subordinate themselves, and he refused it to India.

reason-over-faith.rationale: His philosophical argument rejects self-sufficient naturalism and grounds reason’s reliability in theism.

class-collaboration.rationale: In 1925 he calls the creed of class warfare abominable and says prosperity rests on co-operation among all classes.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: He personally defends public funding for religious teaching in schools and rejects excluding denominational institutions.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He says in 1913 that the deliberate will of the community must prevail at home, yet defended British rule over India against its nationalists.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: In 1920 he calls the view that universal warfare is the best path to progress a misreading of Darwin and a sham philosophy.

separated-powers.rationale: He defends a Second Chamber as the check that stops an unchecked assembly becoming hasty and tyrannical.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: In 1920 he says democracy is most endangered where a state holds elements that are not homogeneous, whether in language, race or religion.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He personally drove permanent emergency powers against Irish agrarian agitation and nationalist organization.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: In 1920 he rejects a League turned into a super-State over sovereign nations as a wild scheme the Covenant never intended.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: While disclaiming superiority, he attributes distinctive governing capacities to Western peoples and endorses their rule over Eastern peoples.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He argues against taking the Church in Wales's endowments, saying a Church is not improved by being deprived of its property.

mixed-constitution.rationale: He praises a Lords of experienced men beside the elected Commons and urges that hereditary and other elements be kept in the Second Chamber.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: He defends a Jewish national home while denying that its agency will exercise political domination over Arabs.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: His 1918 note supports a homeland for the Jews as the remedy for their suffering under unequal citizenship in Europe.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: His stated aim is to diminish the fiscal barriers that hamper Britain's foreign trade as well as to draw the colonies closer, not to shut an imperial bloc off from outsiders.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: In 1911 he says it would be folly to throw aside the hereditary principle in the Second Chamber and that a leaven of heredity is necessary.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He argues British rule benefits peoples he considers unprepared for Western self-government.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: He explicitly says Western self-government cannot simply be implanted into Eastern societies.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: His education scheme combines local public administration with public support for denominational school providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred: his defense of theism as necessary to coherent reason contradicts treating religion as merely compensatory illusion.

historical-land-claim.rationale: His memorandum explicitly gives age-long Zionist traditions greater weight than present Arab inhabitants’ wishes.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He personally prohibited the National League and prosecuted nationalist organizers, though later retreating from plans to silence their press.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: He describes Palestine’s Jewish home as a partial answer to a worldwide Jewish problem, preserving diaspora communities.

second-chamber.rationale: In 1910 and 1913 he wants a stronger Second Chamber, distinct from the Commons, with experience and a check on passing passion.

women-suffrage.rationale: He supports enfranchising women occupiers, expressly rejecting equal voting as an inherent universal right.

national-church-status.rationale: He defended the established Church in Wales against disestablishment and endowment loss as a harm to one communion.

notes:
One historical deduction is marked Inferred. Later Irish treaty acquiescence qualifies earlier unionism. National home is not automatically equated with sovereign statehood. The eugenics speech calls for research and anticipates conscious management of heredity but does not establish a specific compulsory sterilization, marriage prohibition or racial-genetic ability policy; these remain null. The entire statement list was reviewed against full downloaded writing and debates. No positions assigned from aristocratic status, Conservative membership, church affiliation or signature alone. Philosophical theism does not establish scriptural civil law or a particular established-church constitution. Environmental and modern technology propositions lack individual evidence.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 27 answers taken from it, 13 agreed, 2 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Second independent pass, reading his own speeches and essays rather than the first audit's answers. Themes searched: economy (1924 Socialism speech, Economic Notes, 1909 Budget), government (Lords, Parliament Bill, referendum, 1887 crimes bill), world (1916-17 war writings, League of Nations, India, Zionism), society (class war, nationality, Welsh Church, religious education). Left null: tax and welfare detail, gender, ecology, technology, civil liberties beyond Ireland, and policing/defence statements he never addressed. National self-determination and consent are 0 low because he backed European nationality claims while denying them to India. Blocked: Britannica and the Dictionary of Irish Biography sit behind bot walls.
